mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly lists the main components of blood?

options.A: Plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets
options.C: Red blood cells, white blood cells, bone marrow, plasma

mcqs.answer: Plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets
mcqs.explanation: Blood consists of four major components: plasma (the liquid medium), red blood cells (carry oxygen), white blood cells (defence), and platelets (clotting). Options B, C, and D either include non‑blood components or miss one of the four main parts.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand functions of red blood cells
mcqs.question: What is the primary function of red blood cells in the human circulatory system?

options.B: Carry oxygen from the lungs to body tissues
options.C: Form blood clots at sites of injury
options.D: Transport nutrients from the digestive tract

mcqs.answer: Carry oxygen from the lungs to body tissues
mcqs.explanation: Red blood cells contain the protein hemoglobin, which binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it to cells throughout the body. They do not produce antibodies (white blood cells do), form clots (platelets do), or transport nutrients (plasma does).

mcqs.learning_point: Understand functions of white blood cells
mcqs.question: Which statement best distinguishes white blood cells from red blood cells?

options.A: White blood cells contain hemoglobin, while red blood cells do not
options.B: White blood cells are involved in immunity, whereas red blood cells transport oxygen
options.C: White blood cells carry oxygen to tissues, while red blood cells fight infections
options.D: White blood cells are the most abundant cells in blood, unlike red blood cells

mcqs.answer: White blood cells are involved in immunity, whereas red blood cells transport oxygen
mcqs.explanation: White blood cells (leukocytes) protect the body by attacking pathogens, while red blood cells (erythrocytes) primarily transport oxygen. They differ in function, not in hemoglobin content or abundance (red cells are far more numerous).

mcqs.question: If a person suffers a deep cut, which blood component is primarily responsible for stopping the bleeding?
mcqs.explanation: Platelets aggregate at the site of injury, forming a plug and releasing clotting factors that lead to fibrin formation. Red and white blood cells do not form clots, and plasma is the liquid medium that carries them.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a substance that is transported in the plasma portion of blood?
mcqs.explanation: Plasma is the liquid part of blood and carries dissolved nutrients such as glucose, hormones, and waste products. Hemoglobin, platelets, and red blood cells are cellular components, not dissolved in plasma.

mcqs.question: A medical student observes that the right side of the heart receives deoxygenated blood and pumps it to the lungs, while the left side receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and pumps it to the body. Which structure of the heart ensures that these two circuits remain separate?
mcqs.explanation: The interventricular septum (and the atrial septum) separates the right and left chambers, preventing mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood and allowing double circulation. Atria and ventricles are chambers, while valves regulate flow but do not separate the circuits.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes double circulation in humans?

options.A: Blood passes through the heart only once before returning to the body
options.B: Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix in the same circuit
options.C: There are two separate circuits – pulmonary and systemic – that keep oxygenated and deoxygenated blood apart
options.D: The heart pumps blood directly to all body tissues without passing through the lungs

mcqs.answer: There are two separate circuits – pulmonary and systemic – that keep oxygenated and deoxygenated blood apart
mcqs.explanation: Human circulation is double: the pulmonary circuit carries deoxygenated blood from the right heart to the lungs and back, while the systemic circuit carries oxygenated blood from the left heart to the body and back. Options A, B, and D describe single‑circuit or incorrect ideas.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly matches a blood‑vessel type with its characteristic?

options.A: Arteries – carry blood away from the heart and have thin walls
options.B: Veins – carry blood toward the heart and have thick muscular walls
options.C: Capillaries – have walls only one cell thick, allowing exchange of materials
options.D: Veins – have valves that prevent backflow of blood towards the heart

mcqs.answer: Capillaries – have walls only one cell thick, allowing exchange of materials
mcqs.explanation: Capillaries possess walls that are a single endothelial cell layer, facilitating diffusion of gases, nutrients, and wastes. Arteries have thick, muscular walls (not thin), veins have thinner walls and contain valves that prevent backflow toward the periphery (not toward the heart), making options A, B, and D incorrect.
